clue.text: Horse has a pole over

indicators.note: in a down-style reading 'over' means turned over, so the pole is read from end to start

parts.note: a bar is a rod or pole

explanation.surface: A horse is pictured with a pole across it, like a showjumper clearing a rail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a well-known breed of riding horse, so the breed name stands for a horse.

clue.text: Look again at ex-marine at sea on stern of barge

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen

indicators.note: the stern is the back end of a boat, so only the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A former marine aboard a barge, looking back at the water once more.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to inspect or study something a second time, a synonym for 'look again at'.

clue.text: Composer in seventh heaven

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Arthur ..., English composer and Master of the Queen's Music
second meaning: a state of perfect happiness

explanation.surface: A composer is overjoyed, perhaps after a premiere.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Bliss was a twentieth-century English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in seventh heaven is an idiom for supreme joy, which is what bliss names.

clue.text: Craftsman, old master, hasn't finished article

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an old master is a great painter, an artist

explanation.surface: A craftsman, a seasoned expert, has left a piece of work incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, a synonym for craftsman.

clue.text: Girl, one leaving Egyptian port

indicators.note: the letter for one departs from the word, so it is removed

parts.note: the great Mediterranean port of Egypt

explanation.surface: A girl sets off from an Egyptian harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra is a female given name, and crosswords often define names by 'girl'.

clue.text: Nasal tone, Welsh in flavour

indicators.note: one thing sits within another, so the abbreviation goes inside the flavour word

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste

explanation.surface: A nasal accent with a Welsh lilt to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of voice, typical of certain accents.

clue.text: The rub before one gets the needle?

definitions.text: The rub before one gets the needle?

parts.words: The rub before one gets the needle?
parts.note: surface reading: the difficulty or snag before someone becomes irritated

parts.words: The rub before one gets the needle?
parts.note: setter's reading: the antiseptic liquid wiped on the skin before an injection

explanation.walkthrough: 'The rub' suggests 'there's the rub', a problem, and 'gets the needle' means gets annoyed; literally it is a swab before a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical spirit is the British name for rubbing alcohol, used to clean skin before an injection.

clue.text: Obsessive enthusiast on trial with madman

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic, as in 'fitness nut'
a legal case is a trial; 'on' is a link here joining it

explanation.surface: A fanatic stands trial together with a lunatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcase is informal slang for a crazy person, matching madman.

clue.text: Love friend's gemstone

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A lover's or friend's precious stone, perhaps a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is an iridescent precious stone, an example of a gemstone.

clue.text: Heavenly warbler? Yes and no

parts.note: surface reading: an angelic singer from on high
setter's reading: a bird named for paradise, though not literally from heaven nor really a songbird

explanation.walkthrough: The bird's name sounds celestial, hence 'yes', but it is a tropical New Guinea bird famed for plumage, not song, hence 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of paradise are brightly plumed birds whose name links them to heaven.

clue.text: When most TV is watched? Seven, say, on occasion

parts.note: seven is an example of a prime number
an occasion is a time; 'on' joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A viewer asks when the peak TV hours are, answering seven o'clock now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seven' looks like a time of day; it is a number, and 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime time is the evening slot with the biggest television audience.

clue.text: Evil spirit, right, in a well

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the word for healthy, placed within it

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A demon lurks down a well, ready to spring out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a water hole but means in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: An afrit is a powerful malevolent demon in Arabic mythology.

clue.text: Girl exercised daily

indicators.note: exercised suggests the word is worked out and put through its paces into a new form

explanation.surface: A girl who works out every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a female given name, which crosswords define as 'girl'.

clue.text: Drink outside foremost of hotels, then round edge of pool — Hilton's paradise!

indicators.note: the drink wraps around the outside of the hotel letter
the result goes round the pool letter, enclosing it
foremost means the very front, so only the first letter is kept
an edge is a boundary, here the far end, so only the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A hotelier named Hilton sips a drink by the pool of his hotel, calling it paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilton is not the hotel chain but James Hilton, whose novel Lost Horizon invented the hidden valley; H goes in after the S of the drink, then L before its final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the earthly utopia in James Hilton's novel, now a byword for any idyllic hideaway.

clue.text: Just quandaries RAF sorted out

indicators.note: sorted out means rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: The air force has resolved its dilemmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and square is an idiom meaning honestly and justly, so it matches 'just' as an adjective.

clue.text: Left group, one featured in commercial

indicators.note: to be featured in something is to appear within it, so these go inside

explanation.surface: Someone quits a band after appearing in a TV advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb for quitting the group, but it is the definition, an adjective meaning deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means left behind or deserted, used as a past participle.

clue.text: Interrogates searching parties about one, short one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the searching parties wrap round the rest

parts.note: quests are searches, here people sent on them

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Search teams quiz a suspect, one who is a bit short.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone is to interrogate them; both are third-person verbs.

clue.text: More than one theatre employee amazes a star back inside

indicators.note: inside places the turned piece within the other word
going back means reading from the end towards the start

parts.note: a big name is a star

explanation.surface: A theatre crew amazes a star backstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' and 'inside' sit together and read like 'backstage'; they are two separate signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage managers run the backstage side of a production, so they are theatre staff, plural.

clue.text: Hide in SE Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: Someone goes into hiding on an island in the southeast Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it, a verb meaning hide.

clue.text: Told a joke at college and burst into laughter

parts.note: to crack a joke is to tell one
being up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: A student told a joke and fell about laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracked up is an informal phrasal verb for burst out laughing, both in past tense.

clue.text: Knock out, with a left, a small bear

explanation.surface: A boxer floors a little bear with a left hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A left' sounds like a punch, completing the boxing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is often called a koala bear, though it is in fact a marsupial.

clue.text: Pairs off in capital

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Couples head off to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Burglar, one entering the front of factory

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the numeral is placed within
the front is the start, so only the first letter is kept

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks in through the front of a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief steals, and a burglar is a thief who breaks into buildings.

clue.text: Don't eat quickly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go without food

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as advice not to wolf food; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast is both a verb for abstaining from food and an adverb meaning rapidly.

clue.text: Musical — girl takes it in

indicators.note: the girl takes the word in, holding it inside her name

explanation.surface: A girl absorbs a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Drugs in car cost criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Drugs found in a car carry a criminal penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are illegal drugs, both plural nouns.

clue.text: Precious stone, red, male might present

indicators.note: to present in another way means to set out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man might give a precious stone as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: The emerald is a green gem, an example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Band in the south has re-formed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south

indicators.note: re-formed means made again in a new shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A pop group from the south has got back together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.
